prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: Twenty-four healthy adults performed rhythmic left wrist movements while watching a virtual hand under three different conditions: Control, Mirror, and Asymmetric.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Brain activity in the right wrist muscles was measured using a magnetic pulse technique to assess corticospinal excitability.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study found that the type of virtual hand movement affected brain activity in the wrist flexor muscle, but not in the wrist extensor muscle.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Brain signals were stronger in the flexor muscle when the virtual hand matched the real movement during bending, and when it did not match during straightening.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The results suggest that watching different virtual hand movements is linked to specific changes in brain excitability depending on the muscle and movement phase.
facts.subject: humans
